item.title: Deonte Banks Tops Giants Contract List With 14 Pass Breakups
item.description: New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks (2) runs with the ball after an interception during a week 11 NFL football game between New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The New York Giants face a tight window to lock up cornerback Deonte Banks before his contract expires. On Tuesday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN identified Banks as the leading candidate for a contract extension. With 14 pass breakups, the 2023 first-round pick shares the league lead. He enters the final season of his rookie deal, which totals $13.59 million over four years. The team declined his fifth-year option back in May, a move that could cost them dearly now. Banks has turned his career around after being written off by the previous coaching staff. He took the starting job from Paulson Adebo in training camp before the 2026 season. Adebo signed a massive $54 million deal last year, only to lose his spot to a player he was meant to mentor. Alex Wilson from Empire State Media posted on his official X account, “If the depth chart is legit, my god … Paulson Adebo, how did you lose a starting job to Deonte Banks!!!” Setting the Market Price The Denver Broncos recently set a new bar for cornerbacks in their draft class. They signed Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million extension. That breaks down to $16.75 million per year. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan noted, “Greg Newsome got $15.25M. Data points to keep in mind for Deonte Banks’ negotiations.” Newsome, another Giants cornerback, signed a three-year, $46 million deal earlier this month. The Giants should aim for that range to keep their secondary intact without overpaying. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan wrote, “Looks wise for Greg Newsome to lock in his extension eight games into the season.” He added that missing time with a “serious” high-ankle sprain could hurt a player’s market value. Banks has no such injury concerns and is playing at an elite level right now. Waiting until he hits the open market could push his value well past $20 million per year. The Quarterback Question Looms While the defense shines, the quarterback room remains a complex issue. J.J. McCarthy has started 3-1 for the Giants after replacing Jameis Winston. However, the team still holds onto 2025 first-round pick Jaxson Dart. Although a knee injury cost McCarthy his entire rookie year, he holds a 9-5 record as a starter across his first two seasons. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell asked, “What happens when Jaxson Dart is healthy?” The Giants traded only a fifth-round pick to get McCarthy, leaving them with leverage if they choose to move him. In 2027, Brent Sobleski of Bleacher Report projected McCarthy to be the ideal match for the Pittsburgh Steelers. He noted, “For now, Dart remains the presumed long-term preference in New York.” The Steelers need a new quarterback soon as Aaron Rodgers retires after this season. item.title: A year after KKR release, Mustafizur Rahman missing from IPL auction list as 11 Bangladesh players register
item.description: Mustafizur Rahman is not among the 11 Bangladesh players who have registered for the IPL 2027 auction, which will be held in Goa on December 16. The left-arm pacer was released by Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) on the BCCI's instructions last year, a decision that eventually led to Bangladesh withdrawing from the T20 World Cup in India. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia did not specify the reason behind Mustafizur's release at the time, saying only that it was due to "recent developments". The 11 Bangladesh players who have entered the auction are Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Towhid Hridoy and Md Rubel. Stokes enters IPL auction Former England captain Ben Stokes and Australian batter Cameron Bancroft are among the prominent overseas players who have registered for the auction. Stokes, who retired from international cricket earlier this year, has set his base price at Rs 2 crore. The 35-year-old last played in the IPL in 2023, when he featured in two matches for Chennai Super Kings. He has also represented Rajasthan Royals and the now-defunct Rising Pune Supergiant. Bancroft, who has recently sought to clarify his role in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal and responded to claims made by Pat Cummins, has registered at a base price of Rs 75 lakh. The 34-year-old has never played in the IPL but regularly features in the Big Bash League. Australian fast bowler Scott Boland has also registered, although he is not expected to be available for most of the tournament. Japan's Benjamin Ito Davis is among the players from associate nations who could go under the hammer. He has set his base price at Rs 30 lakh. A total of 1,220 players have registered for the auction, including 939 Indians and 281 overseas players. The 10 teams have a maximum of 66 slots to fill, including 25 for overseas players. The list is expected to be cut down significantly before the auction. The registration list includes 184 capped players, 994 uncapped players and 42 players from associate nations. The 10 franchises have retained a total of 184 players. 136154481 Fourteen capped Indian players have also registered for the auction. They are Akash Deep, Avesh Khan, Deepak Chahar, Deepak Hooda, Jaydev Unadkat, Karun Nair, Kuldeep Sen, Mayank Agarwal, Umesh Yadav, Umran Malik, Saransh Jain, Shivam Mavi, Tushar Deshpande and Rahul Tripathi.

item.title: Ben Johnson Keeps D’Andre Swift In Bears Run Game Despite Fumble
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images D’Andre Swift will not lose his spot as the lead back for the Chicago Bears after a costly mistake against the New Orleans Saints. Head coach Ben Johnson made his stance clear on Tuesday. The coach rejected the idea that Swift must work to earn back any trust. He said the running back simply needs to secure the football to keep the offense moving forward. Swift lost his third fumble of the season during the fourth quarter. New Orleans recovered the ball at their own 46-yard line. The 27-year-old runner did not return to the game after that turnover. It marks the second time this year Swift was pulled from a lineup for a fumble. Despite these errors, the coach insists the team will keep relying on its rushing attack. The Trust Factor When asked if Swift needs to regain confidence from the coaching staff, Johnson shut down the notion immediately. “No, he just needs to hold on to the ball and we’ll be fine,” Johnson said, according to ESPN . This comment came after the Bears secured a 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. The victory improved the team’s record, and the coaching staff continues to focus on ball security. Swift has fumbled three times through the first ten games. This is the most he has lost since the 2023 season. Michal Dwojak noted that Swift still holds the head coach’s trust according to RotoBaller. In that game, the veteran back recorded his first touchdown catch of the year. He led the backfield with 15 touches, including two catches for eight yards and a score. Running Game Efficiency The Bears offense relies heavily on moving the chains on the ground. The team ranks third in the league with 142.4 rushing yards per game. However, Johnson was not happy with the efficiency numbers in the recent win. The team rushed for 146 yards against New Orleans, their third-highest total of the year. Yet the average yards per carry fell short of the goal. “We weren’t as consistent running the ball as we had wanted to be coming off the bye, that was a point of emphasis for us,” Johnson said postgame. Swift ran 13 times for 51 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Johnson pointed out that the runners were under four yards a carry. “When I looked at our runners, they were under four yards a carry. That efficiency stat that we talked about, we weren’t hitting that,” Johnson said. Upcoming Matchup Other backs saw action in the game as well. In his first game back after toe and thumb injuries, Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 18 yards. Monangai played 23 offensive snaps compared to Swift’s 28. Salvon Ahmed added six carries to the mix. The coaching staff will look to balance the workload while fixing the ball security issues before the next game. “We’re going to continue to stress that running game,” Johnson said Tuesday. The Bears must prepare for a tough road test against a division rival. The team will face the Detroit Lions on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field.

item.title: FC Barcelona Vs Sabah Line Up: Solutions And Rotations Without Lamine
item.description: FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick will make several rotations for Wednesday's Champions League trip to Baku. Getty Images FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick will make several rotations to his first XI in Wednesday’s Champions League league phase encounter against Sabah. We already knew that Lamine Yamal wouldn’t travel to Baku, after the club released a statement explaining that the youngster is suffering from ankle discomfort. At a prematch press conference on Tuesday, Flick said that a decision was made for the Ballon d’Or candidate to stay behind in Catalunya with an eye on the team’s big picture ambitions. “We’ve played without Lamine in the past; he’s very important to us. Considering our long-term goal, we decided he wouldn’t travel as a precaution,” the manager explained. It was also hinted that Pau Cubarsi might be rested too. “He can play if he’s ready,” Flick explained. “I’ve usually tried to manage him to be as fit as possible. If we can manage the team without him tomorrow, we will. If we can rest him, we will.” This will become a reality, in that Eric Garcia and a Gerard Martin who was monstrous last time out against Villarreal will man central defence while protecting Joan Garcia’s goal. On the flanks, Joao Cancelo starts to the left while Jules Kounde should get the nod over on the right channel despite his lateness to training. The midfield will see Frenkie de Jong rewarded for a strong defensive showing in the 3-2 comeback win against Villarreal and Gavi being handed a rare start. Fermin Lopez is the CAM ahead of the midfield duo as Dani Olmo continues to recover. And on the right wing, in Lamine’s place, it’s Karim Adeyemi. That means that there’s no place for Gabriel Jesus up front, at least not from the offset. Instead, it’s Raphinha as the central number 9 while Anthony Gordon looks to score against a team he netted four past before half time last term while still donning a Newcastle United shirt. What FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick said "It’s [Sabah] a team that likes to play good football. That is its pattern. The most important thing in this match is attitude. It’s the Champions League and we respect every opponent.” FC Barcelona Vs Sabah Expected XI: Garcia; Cancelo, Gerard, Eric, Kounde; De Jong, Gavi, Gordon, Fermin, Adeyemi; Raphinha This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
item.description: Arthur Rinderknech is yet to win an ATP title and reached a highest world ranking of 24th in May [Getty Images] French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test. L'Equipe reported on Wednesday that the current world number 57 is under investigation by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA). It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector". Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision. Rinderknech issued a statement on Instagram in response to L'Equipe's report, saying: "I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation and I have already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal, as is my right." The 31-year-old, who beat current world number one Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, believes he will then be "exonerated of the test refusal allegation". "I have never taken any banned substance and I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always," he added. item.title: Jude Bellingham explains why he’s no match for Zinedine Zidane after shining for Real Madrid
item.description: Jude Bellingham has played down comparisons to Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane after inspiring victory in the Champions League with a sensational goal against PSV. The England international juggled the ball in the air before swiping a volley into the back of the net, leaving fans and teammates in awe, including Bernardo Silva: “It was one of those moments when you just go, ‘Wow!’” The win maintains Madrid’s perfect Champions League record, elevating them to serious contenders to dethrone two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain, while rising up The Independent’s power rankings . And after Mourinho described Bellingham as “without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world,” comparisons continue with one of Madrid’s all-time greatest players: Zidane. But Bellingham was quick to distance himself from the conversation, instead placing the France manager in an entirely different category. "I was a bit surprised, honestly. I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. But normally from there, I'm looking to see who's on as an option to play through,” Bellingham said when asked about his goal before addressing talk that he is on the same level as Zidane. "It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control. Bellingham scored a stunning volley in the second half (Getty) "I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol.” Mourinho was left stunned by his player’s latest impact, pinpointing just what makes him so good. "He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving." “Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,” Mourinho said. “He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.”

item.title: As Farmageddon's streak ends, Kansas State and Iowa State hope it's not for long
item.description: MANHATTAN — When Skylar Thompson first arrived at Kansas State , he knew about the rivalry against Kansas, but when he sat at a team dinner and heard the seniors talk about the importance of beating Iowa State , he learned there was a second rivalry that was almost as important . Winning that game suddenly didn't matter as much for personal pride . Instead, it became about winning for the fanbase, the seniors and the university. Thompson was behind center as a redshirt freshman in 2017 when the Wildcats were down by five against the Cyclones with eight seconds left from the one-yard line. Thompson looked to his left, and no one was open as he scrambled that way. With a defender in his face, he changed direction to the other side of the field. He ran, seemingly forever, until he found Isaiah Zuber in the back of the endzone as time expired . Wildcats win. "That was probably one of my most fond memories at K-State," Thompson said. Nicknamed "Farmageddon" for the agricultural roots of being two land-grant universities, Kansas State and Iowa State have played the longest uninterrupted continuous series in college football, having played each season since 1917. The 110th-straight game between the two will be played on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1 p.m. CT at Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, Iowa. Saturday will also mark the end of the uninterrupted series, as the two are not scheduled to play next season. "We definitely wanted to play it," K-State athletic director Gene Taylor said. "But we knew that everybody was gonna get to play a second rival. We kind of had to take our lumps and agree to the way the scheduling matrix turned out." When the Big 12 added Arizona, Arizona State , Colorado and Utah to expand the league to 16 teams, the reconfigured scheduling matrix chose four "protected" rivalries that wouldn't go away, and Kansas State-Kansas was one of them. That put Farmageddon on the chopping block. When the matrix was released ahead of the 2024 season, it was known the Wildcats' annual game against the Cyclones would end in 2027. A new matrix will need to be developed ahead of the 2028 season, which could see the return of the game sooner rather than later. That's something Taylor expects to happen. With all of the changes in the sport, especially with the 24-team College Football Playoff that will begin in 2027, scheduling will be at the forefront. "I think it may not be as long of a hiatus as we think it was; in essence, there was gonna be a period of 2-3 years where we weren't going to play," Taylor said. "We may have to rethink the entire scheduling model here coming up. I think our fanbase wanted to keep it; there's no question. I think there's a lot of reasons to keep it in the future." Farmageddon predated the Big 8, let alone the Big 12, beginning in 1917 when K-State and Iowa State were both members of a previous iteration of the Missouri Valley Conference. item.title: Bills vs Chiefs prediction, key matchups in Thanksgiving showdown
item.description: ORCHARD PARK - The No. 1 seed in the AFC will not be decided Thursday night when the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in a Thanksgiving showdown befitting one of the biggest national TV windows there is on the NFL schedule. But for the 9-1 Bills in particular, already starting with a one-game advantage on the 8-2 Chiefs, if they can find their way to a victory, they are going to be set up in prime position to grab that elusive spot which they have not enjoyed since the 1993 season. A win would provide Buffalo an important head-to-head tiebreaker advantage meaning the Bills would technically be 2.5 games ahead of Kansas City with six to play. With the Jaguars and Bengals suffering rather inexplicable Week 11 losses, they each have three losses, so Buffalo’s main competition would be the Broncos who go into their Black Friday game in Pittsburgh with an 8-2 record. Flip it around, though, and a Chiefs victory pulls them even with the Bills and gives Kansas City the head-to-head tiebreaker, immediately moving the Chiefs ahead of Buffalo. Denver could also move past the Bills with a win while the Jaguars and Bengals would be just one loss behind. In its promotional material for the game, NBC referred to Bills vs. Chiefs as the “Rivalry of the Decade” and ranked it as the best non-division rivalry since the NFL’s playoff format was altered in 1990, putting it in the same class as Colts-Patriots in the 2000s, and 49ers-Cowboys in the 1990s. They have split 10 games counting the postseason, there have been six one-score games in the bunch, and the teams rank 1-2 in victories in the 2020s, the Bills at 82 and the Chiefs 80. Yeah, the stakes are enormous. item.description: BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football took another tumble in the College Football Playoff rankings. The Hoosiers (9-2, 6-2 Big Ten) dropped six spots to No. 14 , below all the other Big Ten contenders and outside the cut line for the 12-team field. Hunter Yurachek the Arkansas athletic director who serves as the CFP selection committee chair, pointed to several key factors to explain IU's drop on Tuesday night. Here's a look at Yurachek's explanation: More: Indiana football LT Carter Smith's tattoos tell the tale of an unforgettable journey Oregon and Iowa are 'playing really well right now.' Indiana is not. Oregon and Iowa seem to be peaking at the right time and impressed the CFP committee with their recent four-game win streaks. Ducks backup quarterback Dylan Raiola settled into the starting job and helped his team win by an average of 20.8 points over their last four games while the Hawkeyes have only allowed four touchdowns during that stretch. Yurachek noted IU's recent string of one-possession games and how the Hoosiers got tripped up against Washington. "Those games have been dominated by Oregon and by Iowa, and Indiana has had that series of six consecutive one-score games three out of the last four that have been in overtime," Yurachek said. "And they've found ways to win those games, and kudos to them for doing so, but this weekend in Washington it caught up with them." While Yurachek didn't get into specifics, Indiana also faces continued uncertainty at quarterback and a growing number of injury concerns, including multiple starters on the offensive line. CFP committee credits Oregon and Iowa for wins over common opponents The committee puts a lot of weight into common opponents when they don't have any head-to-head results to deliberate over. "Iowa and Indiana both lost at home to Ohio State. You've got another common opponent in Iowa, went to Washington and won by two touchdowns, and Indiana of course went there this weekend and lost by three." item.title: Hillsdale Academy soccer athletes earn six all-state honors
item.description: HILLSDALE — Hillsdale Academy boys soccer capped off another successful fall season with six players earning Division 4 all-state recognition from the Michigan High School Soccer Coaches Association. More: Youngman family runs together, bonds together The Colts finished the 2026 season with a 15-4-2 overall record, capturing their seventh consecutive district championship and reaching the Division 4 regional championship game for the first time since 2020. Junior midfielder Danny Aburto-Rodriguez led the Colts’ postseason honors with a second-team all-state selection. Fellow junior midfielder and cousin Rene Rodriguez earned third-team all-state recognition. Four additional Colts received honorable mention honors, including senior forward Justin Busby, senior defender Hudson Mackie, senior midfielder Andrew Richards and junior goalkeeper Robert Whalen. The six honorees helped lead Hillsdale Academy through another memorable postseason run under longtime head coach Neal Brady. Season review The Colts captured their seventh consecutive district title with a dramatic 3-2 double-overtime victory over Jackson Christian on Oct. 24. Busby delivered the championship-winning goal off an assist from Rene Rodriguez less than a minute into the second overtime period. The victory also marked Brady’s 300th-career coaching win. Hillsdale Academy followed its district championship with an 8-0 shutout of Ypsilanti Arbor Prep in the regional semifinals. Busby scored five goals in the victory, helping the Colts advance to their first regional final appearance in six years. The Colts’ season ended with a 2-0 loss to familiar postseason rival Grosse Pointe Woods University Liggett in the Division 4, Region 15 championship on Oct. 29. Busby, who helped lead the Colts’ offense throughout their championship run, reflected on the relationships he built with his teammates. “We, at the end of the season, became more than just teammates. We became brothers,” Busby said. “This is probably the closest our team’s been since I’ve been here.” The Colts now turn their attention toward 2027, returning both Rodriguez midfielders and Whalen in goal while saying goodbye to a senior class that helped extend one of the program’s most successful stretches. item.title: Missouri faces Oklahoma offense that's found new life in November
item.description: Film study on Oklahoma in the Mizzou football defensive meeting room isn’t reaching much outside of the month of November. The Tigers (7-4, 4-4 SEC) will take on Oklahoma (7-5, 5-3) on Saturday on Faurot Field to round out the regular season. Win, and the Tigers will finish in the top half of the SEC. They’ll almost certainly finish the regular season ranked in the top 25 in all the major polls. Eli Drinkwitz has contract implications on the line , too, as an eighth regular season automatically extends his deal by one year. The matchup against the Sooners is going to bring the typical challenges on defense and special teams. Brent Venables’ defense is, as is usually the case, among the better statistical units in the conference. Oklahoma has the SEC’s leading punt returner, Isaiah Sategna III, who has returned two punts for touchdowns. But a new challenge has emerged. The once-woebegone OU offense has found a groove late in the season. Oklahoma made a change at offensive coordinator on Nov. 2, firing Ben Arbuckle and moving Jason Witten into an interim play-calling role. Since then, the Sooners have won three straight games, guaranteeing they’ll finish SEC play with a winning record, beating Florida, Ole Miss , and Texas A&M in succession. The difference? “I think they've committed to the run game,” MU head coach Eli Drinkwitz said. “They're committed to an identity of what they're trying to do in the pass game, and then they're utilizing Mateer’s legs as an extra weapon, and so I think anytime you have those three things coming together — identity in the run game, known pass game, you know, using that quarterback as that primary runner — that's very difficult on defense. Very difficult to figure out how you're going to stop the run.” That assessment checks out. Before the OC change, Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer was averaging nine carries per game for 32 rushing yards per game. Over the Sooners’ unbeaten last three matchups, he’s taken an average of 13.3 carries for 71.3 yards on the ground per game. “With a running quarterback, they have plus-one runs, and then he can also throw the ball pretty well,” MU linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez said. “So, you’ve got to be able to defend his legs and his arms. So, it's just kind of the battle you have to go through when you face a dual-threat quarterback.” Getting Mateer more involved on the ground has seemingly opened up the rest of the OU offense. The Sooners were struggling earlier in the season. In their first four games against Power-conference teams, they only managed 13 points once. Since the offensive coordinator change, Oklahoma has won 23-7, 24-17 and 28-7. OU has averaged 161.3 yards of rushing offense on 42 carries per outing in November. item.title: Championship weekend has arrived, time for some football state finals picks
item.description: For the first time in a long time, northern Michigan is left out of the Thanksgiving weekend party at Ford Field. The MHSAA football state championships will take place for all eight 11-player divisions this weekend, but you won’t find a representative out of northern Michigan, or even the Upper Peninsula, for the first time in a while. Whether it’s been Kingsley or Traverse City St. Francis, Menominee or Negaunee, it feels like we’ve had someone to represent for a while. We’ve even had Cadillac, Traverse City Central and Glen Lake fighting for recent titles. The closest we get in 2026 is Beal City, though anyone that considers them northern Michigan has a Detroit area code in front of their phone number. But, even without a team in the final dance, there are plenty of great games to look forward to and some of the best players in the state in action ahead. Games will be played on Friday and Saturday, Nov. 27-28 at Ford Field in Detroit, with game times listed below. Four games will take place each day. While we don’t have any local teams playing, there are plenty of familiar teams to pick from below. DIVISION 1 Detroit Catholic Central (12-1) vs. Romeo (13-0) 7 p.m., Saturday What a story Romeo has been this season, capped by a 30-29 win over powerhouse Detroit Cass Tech a week ago, pulling ahead on a 2-point conversion inside two minutes. Now, they get another state powerhouse and the defending Division 1 state champs. There’s so much firepower on this Catholic Central team, from five-star Texas Tech commit Gideon Gash and running back Ryan Jaafar, to an experienced QB in Duke Banta. Romeo is a tough team, but it feels like the great story ends here. Catholic Central 38, Romeo 20 DIVISION 2 Orchard Lake St. Mary’s (10-3) vs. Muskegon Mona Shores (12-1) 7 p.m., Friday St. Mary’s has won two straight titles, while Mona Shores pulled in two straight back in 2019-20. So, both programs aren’t new to Ford Field by any means. The difference here feels like the experience and talent of St. Mary QB Jabin Gonzalez, who has so much talent to work with, led by North Carolina commit Chad Willis. Lorenzo Barber and Brannon Hardy have also been big. It’s a rematch from Week 1 of the season in a 35-27 win for St. Mary’s and they’ll prove to be the better team again in a three-peat. Orchard Lake St. Mary’s 26, Muskegon Mona Shores 20 DIVISION 3 Zeeland West (11-2) vs. Harper Woods (11-2) 12:30 p.m., Saturday After a 2024 state title, West came up just short a year ago of making Ford Field, but they’re back and as powerful as ever, highlighted by a 42-26 win over DeWitt a week ago. Harper Woods has arguably the best player in the state in Oregon commit Dakota Guerrant, along with the likes of Deandre Bidden and AJ Henley, both juniors with Michigan offers. Woods also has a powerful line up front to match West, which is the main reason to pick them here. item.title: Ohio State-Michigan football history, head-to-head record ahead of The Game
item.description: The Game, college football's biggest rivalry and one of the most notable annual battles in North American sports, is back. Ohio State and Michigan will play on Nov. 28 in the 129th year of the rivalry. Last year, Ohio State beat Michigan 27-9 and snapped a four-game losing streak to the Wolverines dating back to a 42-27 loss to Michigan in 2021. This year's rivalry game will have a different feel . Ohio State and Michigan combine for nine losses this season, with the 7-4 Buckeyes and 6-5 Wolverines essentially out of the hunt for a College Football Playoff spot. More: Ohio State football has one remote path to the Big Ten title game. Here's the scenario "The Game is still The Game," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said on Nov. 24. "We’re playing on Saturday. And it means everything to us." The two schools' storied rivalry includes fights , historic upsets and longstanding traditions leading up to The Game, including Ohio State fans crossing out the letter 'M' in Columbus. When did the Ohio State-Michigan rivalry begin? item.title: WSL makes agreement with clubs to avoid gambling sponsors
item.description: WSL Football, the organisation responsible for operating the top two tiers of women’s football in the UK, has reached an agreement in principle for its clubs not to make sponsorship deals with betting companies. Instead, the organisation has agreed to pursue sponsorship deals with brands from different industries, reports The Athletic . The outlet states that six additional sponsorship opportunities were made available ahead of the 2024/25 season, and these were filled by Apple, Airbnb, British Gas, Mercedes, Tesco and WTW. While the agreement applies to WSL Football’s own commercial partnerships, it does not stop individual WSL or WSL2 clubs from signing sponsorship deals with gambling companies. Rather, it sets a different direction for WSL Football’s league-level partnerships, giving the leagues the chance to shape their own commercial future. The organisation wants to continue aiding the growth of the women’s domestic game, while combating issues such as player welfare, gambling-related online abuse and fluctuating attendances. The changes also come at a time when English football is starting to take a wider look at gambling and related sponsorships. At the start of this season, the Premier League’s voluntary ban on betting sponsors appearing on the front of match-day shirts came into effect, while the Premier League, EFL, FA and WSL also introduced a Code of Conduct for gambling-related sponsorship agreements in 2024. Nevertheless, betting companies still feature prominently among sponsors at clubs throughout the top divisions in the men’s game, with Betway signing a deal with Manchester United and clubs such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest also agreeing new deals over the summer.

There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. item.description: Fin Smith makes a break in last weekend's 37-12 win over New Zealand [Getty Images] With a grin and an expletive, Fin Smith describes Ben Earl as "greedy". "It takes some doing to get just one carry when he's on the pitch," jokes Smith to BBC Sport. "He hogs them all." Earl's performance in Saturday's win over New Zealand certainly caught the eye. The number eight carried a phenomenal 32 times in the 37-12 victory, more than twice as much as anyone else on the pitch. But, further down the standings, Smith also stood out. He carried the ball 11 times against the All Blacks, the third-highest total of any England player. That stat comes with context. The fly-half racked up his total in just 55 minutes on the pitch before cramp forced him to the bench. For Smith, 5ft 10in tall and less than 14 stone, such physicality is not unusual. A fortnight before beating New Zealand, against Australia, he carried nine times, his team's fourth-highest total. According to stats from Oval Insights, he has carried more than any other fly-half in a Six Nations side this year. If you include Rugby Championship teams in the mix, only three fly-halves - New Zealand's Richie Mo'unga, South Africa's Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Argentina's Tomas Albornoz - have backed themselves more with the ball. Smith admits he does not have the athletic ability of some of those rivals. But the Northampton man says his attempts to play through the defence, rather than in front of them, helps him lead the team to a more effective attack. "I do like the physical side," he adds. "It gets me into games, but also I think it is just my character. "I would hate to be someone that is asking everyone else to go and be physical and put their body on the line, if I wasn't particularly willing to do it. I think that's how I've been brought up." With George Furbank, Henry Slade and Seb Atkinson all able to step in at first receiver, Smith being buried at the bottom of the breakdown is a price England are able to pay for a phase or two. "It's important for me to be a threat myself," he adds. "The way we're playing at Northampton and England, and the way I feel like teams attack best when I'm in them, is when there are almost no numbers on backs. "You play as quickly as possible and whoever ends up in the slots just does that job. You've got to be interchangeable. "If the right thing to do is carry or the right thing to do is hit the breakdown then so be it, and then someone else can drop in as the first playmaker. item.title: THERE IS NO “10/10, BUT”
item.description: THERE IS NO “10/10, BUT” On 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women , Juventus launches THERE IS NO “10/10, BUT” , an awareness campaign aimed at its community, with a particular focus on younger generations and their first romantic relationships. The aim is to encourage people to recognise controlling and possessive behaviours that are mistaken for signs of love, excused as jealousy or normalised within a relationship. The campaign draws inspiration from a popular social media trend: “a 10/10, but…” , which involves rating an ideal partner while joking about minor flaws, habits or incompatibilities. The video features a number of young players from the Juventus Women’s First Team and Under-19 side , taking part in a narrative that speaks directly to their generation. The video begins by following the familiar format of the trend, with light-hearted, everyday situations being rated in a relaxed atmosphere. Then something changes. When behaviours such as demanding to know where a partner is at all times, getting angry when they go out with friends, checking their phone or restricting their freedom are mentioned, the trend comes to a halt. The closing message makes this shift in perspective clear: THERE IS NO “10/10, BUT.” SOME BEHAVIOURS ARE SIMPLY NOT ACCEPTABLE. It is not, therefore, about measuring how "perfect" a person or a relationship is, but about learning to recognise behaviours that cannot be accepted or justified. Because jealousy is not proof of love, possessiveness is not a form of protection, and restricting another person's freedom is never an act of affection. A LOOK AT RELATIONSHIPS AMONG YOUNGER GENERATIONS Further context for the campaign comes from the findings of the 2026 TEEN Survey , which focuses on Italian teenagers aged 14 to 19 and was conducted by Fondazione Libellula . The Foundation has been working with Juventus since 2022 to prevent and combat gender-based violence and all forms of discrimination. The findings reveal how a culture that normalises jealousy and controlling behaviour in romantic relationships remains widespread even among younger generations, including in the way relationships are portrayed on social media: 85% have seen posts or videos portraying jealousy or controlling behaviour in a relationship as normal; 34% believe jealousy is a sign of love; 36% consider it normal to impose restrictions on their partner. It is with this awareness in mind that THERE IS NO “10/10, BUT” was created. Having different tastes, habits or opinions is part of a relationship. Controlling another person, restricting their freedom or deciding what they can and cannot do is not. And recognising the difference is a responsibility we all share. item.description: Oscar Piastri finished on the podium at the chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix . I think the ups have been back at the level that they should be, and the downs obviously are not where they should be. McLaren slammed for treating Piastri as 'second fiddle' to Norris in Las Vegas Former F1 driver and F1 TV analyst Jolyon Palmer was not happy with how Piastri was told to play second fiddle to Norris in Las Vegas. item.title: Sri Lanka beat Ireland in Emerging Nations final
item.description: Sri Lanka eased to victory in the final in Ajman [Getty Images] ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy final, Ajman Sri Lanka 99-4 (12.4 overs): Dulani 44*, Kavindi 25; McCartney 2-16 Ireland 96 all out (19.3 overs): Dalzell 24, Little 15; Sandeepani 4-13 Sri Lanka win by six wickets Scorecard Ireland Women suffered a disappointing defeat in the final of the Emerging Nations Trophy as they fell to a six-wicket loss against Sri Lanka in Ajman. Sri Lanka won the toss and opted to field first, with Ireland enduring a difficult start which they failed to recover from. Sathya Sandeepani starred for Sri Lanka as she claimed four wickets from just 13 balls. Two of those wickets came in the first three overs, with Irish captain Gaby Lewis out in the first over and Lara Mitz in the third. Ireland were on 54-6 midway through the 12th over as the wickets continued to tumble. Louise Little exited in the seventh over after providing 15 runs off 17 balls including two fours with Amy Hunter (10), Laura Delany (seven) and Abbi Harrison (five) following soon after. Georgina Dempsey managed 13 runs before she was run out by Vishmi Gunaratne, with Sandeepani then taking the next two wickets from Cara Murray and Ireland's top scorer Alana Dalzell, who managed 24 runs from 25 balls. When Kia McCartney exited, Ireland were all out for just 96 by 19.3 overs and Sri Lanka surpassed that target in just 12.4 overs to claim a comfortable win. Sri Lanka made a steady start but lost Sanjana Kavindi (25) and captain Harshitha Samarawickrama, who failed to register any runs, in consecutive deliveries from McCartney in the fifth over. They were on just 69-4 by the ninth over as Murray claimed two more wickets from Gunaratne and Kaushini Nuthayangana, but Imesha Dulani then led their charge. She registered an unbeaten 44 off 25 deliveries, including four boundaries and two sixes while Kavisha Dilhari also added an unbeaten 16 from 10 balls as Sri Lanka finished with 99-4 to take home the trophy.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
